subcategory_text: Privacy risk is re-evaluated on an ongoing basis and as key factors, including the organization's business environment (e.g., introduction of new technologies), governance (e.g., legal obligations, risk tolerance), data processing, and systems/products/services change
informative_references: NIST SP 800-39: Managing Information Security Risk (continuous monitoring framing)
NIST SP 800-137: Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information Systems and Organizations
NIST PF 1.0 Core (January 2020): GV.MT-P1 (verified in NIST-Privacy-Framework-V1.0-Core.xlsx row 38)
GDPR Art. 35 (Data protection impact assessment), Art. 36 (Prior consultation)
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.7 (Threat intelligence), A.5.30 (ICT readiness for business continuity)
Aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-05 (inherent risk re-evaluation)
implementation_examples: Schedule periodic privacy-risk re-evaluations at defined intervals

Trigger privacy-risk re-evaluation when key factors change: new technologies adopted, governance changes (legal/risk tolerance), new data-processing activities, or new systems/products/services deployed
Document the re-evaluation output as input to enterprise risk management processes
assessment_objectives: Determine whether a defined cadence exists for privacy-risk re-evaluation
Determine whether triggers for ad-hoc re-evaluation are documented and operationalised
Determine whether re-evaluation outputs feed back into enterprise risk management
Determine whether changes to the key-factor set (business, governance, processing, systems) are detected and acted upon
